source.title: Disentangling Polysemantic Neurons with a Null-Calibrated Polysemanticity Index and Causal Patch Interventions

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper presents PSI as a tool for investigating polysemanticity and superposition, and reports measurements of prototype structure in ResNet-50. It does not test whether sparse features exceed dimensional capacity, whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity, or whether the features are overlapping directions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own measurements of polysemanticity-related structure and causal patch swaps, recorded below as findings that fit none of the listed versions. It does not test feature sparsity, feature importance, feature-versus-dimension counts, capacity allocation, LLM representations, SAEs, or feature dimensionality. Background claims and cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a metric paper. It introduces PSI and reports the metric's own validation in one pretrained ResNet-50: null AUROCs, depth trend, patch swaps and sensitivity checks. It measures top-activation cluster structure, i.e. polysemanticity, not superposition. It does not measure feature counts versus dimensions, sparsity, capacity allocation, direction geometry, SAEs or feature dimensionality. The subject is a CNN, not an LLM, so V4 does not apply. The claim that deeper layers 'pack complex concepts into fewer neurons using techniques like superposition' (Sec 5.2) is asserted, not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also interpret the depth trend as deeper layers packing concepts into fewer neurons 'using techniques like superposition', which they assert without testing. Their robustness claims are partly contradicted by their own appendix.
record.recipe_differences: Measures top-activating image patches with a null-calibrated clustering, label-alignment, and CLIP-semantic index, plus patch-swap interventions; it does not use the original toy-model setup or measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: PSI rankings vary with the number of top patches K; semantic distinctness scores vary with the CLIP text encoder.

fits_no_version.finding: In pretrained ResNet-50, layer4 channels have higher PSI (decomposable top-activation clusters) than layer3 (KS p≪1e-6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured polysemanticity of vision CNN channels increases with depth.

fits_no_version.finding: PSI and its components separate real channels from randomized nulls. The layer4 full-PSI AUROC is reported inconsistently (0.987 vs 0.599).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Null-calibrated cluster metrics distinguish real neuron activation structure from chance.

fits_no_version.finding: For 10 high-PSI layer4 neurons, aligned prototype patch swaps raised activation by +0.15, while non-aligned and random patches lowered it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Discovered prototype clusters of polysemantic CNN neurons are causally effective inputs.

fits_no_version.finding: Example channels show split versus coherent top activations, and most high-PSI channels select 2–3 clusters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Polysemantic CNN channels typically respond to a small number of discrete prototypes.

fits_no_version.finding: PSI rankings depend on top-K and on the text encoder (ρ≈0.21 across encoders).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Polysemanticity scores from activation clustering are sensitive to analysis choices.

record.problems: The layer4 full-PSI AUROC is inconsistent: Table 1 gives 0.987, while Section 5.1 and Figure 2b give 0.599; the abstract says approximately 0.99. The main text and appendix also report differing PSI-ranking correlations for changes in K. The causal patch-swap study uses 10 selected high-PSI neurons, and the null distributions use M = 20 samples per component. Results are limited to one pretrained CNN and do not directly measure feature capacity, sparsity, importance, or direction geometry.
record.rows_left_out: No reported claim-relevant outcomes were left out. Cited background findings and method details without reported outcomes are not rows.

untested.parts: All parts: no toy model, no sparsity sweep, no feature/dimension counts, no geometry.
Whether capacity competition causes the observed polysemanticity. The depth trend is attributed to superposition-like packing without any test.
No test of non-capacity causes. The cited claim that L1 or noise can cause polysemanticity is background only.
No LLM analysis and no SAE. The ResNet-50 polysemanticity measurements are outside V4's named system type.
Cluster counts K̂ of 2–3 describe activation-patch clusters, not feature dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: Internal inconsistencies: layer4 PSI AUROC is 0.987 or 0.599, and the K-sensitivity numbers differ between main text and appendix. Null estimates use M=20 samples per component. The patch-swap study uses only 10 selected neurons. None of this bears on any version.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, sparse feature counts relative to dimensions, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, and sparsity-dependent geometry.
Whether capacity competition causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
The paper measures polysemanticity-related structure but does not establish that it arises without capacity pressure or identify an alternative cause.
No LLM neuron-distribution or SAE feature-recovery analysis.
No test of whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
No test of whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: ResNet-50

rows.measure: Spearman rank correlation of PSI rankings
rows.note: Main text says correlation increases toward the K = 50 baseline.
